Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations. Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.

Consideration to Adopt the 2025 Urban Water Management Plan and 2025 Water Shortage Contingency Plan. Recommendations: 1) Open the public hearing to receive comments and close the hearing following completion of comments; and 2) Approve Resolution No. 2026-UB-04 adopting the 2025 Urban Water Management Plan and the 2025 Water Shortage Contingency Plan and file with the DWR by July 1, 2026.

Update on Senate Bill 707 Brown Act Requirements and Consideration of Resolution Approving a Policy for the Telephonic or Internet Service Disruptions and Removal of Disruptive Members of the Public Recommendations: 1) Discuss and provide direction regarding the implementation of SB 707 requirements; 2) Adopt Resolution No. 2026-UB-05, adopting a Disruption of Telephonic or Internet Service and Removal of Disruptive Members of the Public During Council Meetings Policy pursuant to Government Code Section 54953.4; and 3) Determine reasonable efforts for outreach to encourage participation in Utility Board meetings.

F.
SCHEDULED ITEMS - JOINT UTILITY BOARD/CITY COUNCIL
1.
Consideration to Approve Joint Resolution No. 2026-C28 Establishing Utility Rate Setting Procedures for Water Rates Under Proposition 218 and Assembly Bill 2257, and Authorizing a Suspension of the Water Utility Users Tax Under Azusa Municipal Code Section 70-268; Receive Water Cost of Service Study Results; and Authorization to Mail Notice of Public Hearing to be Held July 27, 2026, for Water Rate Adjustment Recommendations: 1) Approve Joint Resolution 2026-C28 of the City of Azusa and Utility Board of the City of Azusa, establishing Utility Rate setting procedures for Water Rates under Proposition 218 and Assembly Bill 2257, and authorizing a suspension of the Water Utility Users Tax under Azusa Municipal Code section 70-268; and 2) Approve the attached public hearing notice of the proposed water rate adjustment to increase rates by 16% in FY 2026/27, 16% in FY 2027/28, 16% in FY 2028/29, and 4% annually in FY 2029/30 through FY 2030/31; and 3) Authorize Staff to print and mail the Notice of Public Hearing to all water customers and property owners, with the public hearing to be held July 27, 2026, at the regular Utility Board meeting time and place, and the notice to be mailed no less than 45 days prior to the public hearing to comply with Proposition 218 and AB 2257.
